description: Environmental condition classifications, interpretations, and recommended actions for Stevia cultivation, compiled from horticultural and agronomic research sources for use in SPROUT's rule-based/agentic recommendation engine.

classifications.label: optimal
classifications.interpretation: Nutrient uptake and root health are at their best; ideal for steviol glycoside development.
classifications.recommendation: Maintain current soil pH; no amendment needed.

classifications.label: too_acidic
classifications.interpretation: Acidic soil limits nutrient availability (calcium, magnesium) and can stunt growth.
classifications.recommendation: Apply agricultural lime or dolomite to raise pH gradually; retest after 1-2 weeks.

classifications.label: too_alkaline
classifications.interpretation: Alkaline soil reduces iron and micronutrient uptake, causing chlorosis.
classifications.recommendation: Apply elemental sulfur or organic compost to lower pH gradually.

classifications.label: optimal
classifications.interpretation: Ideal daytime growth range; supports steady vegetative growth and leaf sweetness.
classifications.recommendation: Maintain current conditions; monitor peak daytime heat.

classifications.label: cool_suboptimal
classifications.interpretation: Below ~60F at night suppresses growth; prolonged exposure risks stunting.
classifications.recommendation: Advise row covers or activate heating control; delay watering.

classifications.label: frost_critical
classifications.interpretation: Below ~45F, stevia will not tolerate exposure; risk of plant death.
classifications.recommendation: Trigger critical alert; recommend immediate frost protection.

classifications.label: heat_stress
classifications.interpretation: Excess heat causes leaf scorch and increased water demand; can reduce sweetness.

classifications.label: optimal
classifications.interpretation: Matches high-mountain native cultivation conditions (~73% RH) linked to best growth performance (R2>0.85).
classifications.recommendation: Maintain current humidity; no action needed.

classifications.label: low_dry_stress
classifications.interpretation: Low humidity increases transpiration stress; can cause leggy growth or leaf curling.
classifications.recommendation: Activate misting/humidification if available; increase watering frequency slightly.

classifications.label: high_fungal_risk
classifications.interpretation: Excess humidity with poor airflow raises risk of wilt and leaf spot diseases.
classifications.recommendation: Improve ventilation; reduce misting; inspect for fungal spotting.

classifications.label: optimal
classifications.interpretation: Full sun exposure supports dense, bushy growth and maximum leaf yield.

classifications.label: insufficient
classifications.interpretation: Partial shade causes spindly growth and fewer leaves (lower yield).
classifications.recommendation: Relocate grow lights closer or extend photoperiod via supplemental LED lighting.

classifications.label: optimal
classifications.interpretation: Soil consistently moist but well-drained; top inch dry before rewatering.

classifications.label: too_dry
classifications.interpretation: Top inch and subsoil fully dry; risk of drought stress and reduced yield.

classifications.label: waterlogged
classifications.interpretation: Standing water or saturated soil; high risk of root rot and wilt disease.
classifications.recommendation: Halt irrigation; improve drainage; inspect roots for rot.
